_doc: Which language a NON-SPECIFIC code routes to. This is CLI configuration, not a fact about any language: it records what Champollion does when a user types a code that does not identify one language, and every entry is an editorial decision that could reasonably have gone another way.
_whyItIsNotACardField: A card asserts what SOURCES say about a language. 'When someone types zh, give them Mandarin' is not something Glottolog or SIL says — it is a routing choice we make, and putting it on a card would dress our decision up as an upstream fact. It lives here so it can be argued with.
_derivedRoutingIsElsewhere: Codes that unambiguously identify one language — fr to fra, am to amh, and 82 others — are DERIVED from SIL's own ISO 639-1 column and projected as the codeAlias parameter. Only the ambiguous cases are listed here.
status: carried forward from the previous corpus, AWAITING FOUNDER REVIEW
reviewNote: Each of these picks ONE individual language to stand for a macrolanguage. That is defensible and it is a choice: routing 'ar' to Modern Standard Arabic serves most callers and serves none of the 30-odd other Arabic varieties. The alternative — refusing to route and asking the caller to be specific — is also defensible. Nobody has ruled.

ar.rationale: Modern Standard Arabic for the Arabic macrolanguage. The variety with the most MT support and written material.

ara.rationale: Same decision, reached by the macrolanguage code rather than its ISO 639-1.

zh.rationale: Mandarin for the Chinese macrolanguage. Note this routes past written-form questions (Hans/Hant) that a locale tag would carry.

no.rationale: Bokmål for Norwegian. Nynorsk (nno) is a co-official written standard, so this is the sharpest of these choices.

sq.rationale: Tosk Albanian for the Albanian macrolanguage — the basis of the standard language.
